Subject: Re: Intro — evaluating Redwood on AWS (MAP request)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — infra team liked the latency profiles. We need a mutual action plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to a Private Offer structure in AWS Marketplace so procurement can see when credits convert to committed spend. Key asks from my side:
- A two-week eval sprint, followed by a 60-day pilot window.
- Credit tranche on sign (N USD), then staged credits released after two milestone ramps (50% and 80% of target RPS).
- Clear trigger points for a first-year commit and discount thresholds.

Can you put a runbook together with the milestones, the proposed commit cadence, and what the Private Offer would look like (staged commit amounts / discount matrix)? Procurement also needs SOC2 summary and a sample PO template.

Thanks,
Samir

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — evaluating Redwood on AWS (MAP request)

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. I put together a draft MAP and an example Private Offer structure that maps credit sweeps to milestone velocity. Summary below and file attached.

Highlights (see MAP_v1.xlsx):
- Eval sprint (Day 0–14): Redwood provides $35k eval credits on sign to cover sandbox + pilot load tests.
- Pilot window (Day 15–75): incremental usage; we propose two sweep checkpoints at Day 30 and Day 60 tied to observed RPS and token consumption. If NovaProd hits >=50% of target RPS by Day 30, Redwood releases an additional $25k credit and unlocks a 5% discount tier on the Private Offer.
- Commit triggers:
  * Commitment A (sign + Day 75): first-year minimum commit = $600k; if Day 60 usage >=80% of target, apply additional 7% discount (cumulative).
  * Velocity-based uplift: if average weekly token/sec growth > 20% during the pilot we reduce ramp schedule to compress commits into Q4.
- Failure-to-ramp fallback: if Day 75 targets not met, credits expire and we offer an extended pilot with a smaller commit or a pro-rated bridge credit.

Attachments included: MAP_v1.xlsx (milestone table + sample private offer lines), NovaProd_AWSUsage_Sample.csv (our sample analysis), Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf.

Next steps I suggest: procurement review the MAP and confirm the acceptance criteria for the two sweep checkpoints; Redwood to produce a draft Private Offer in AWS Marketplace once we align on commit amounts. Will also pull in legal if there are specific billing terms.

Thanks — attaching a short running checklist in the spreadsheet for easy handoff.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Sales Manager, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx ; NovaProd_AWSUsage_Sample.csv ; Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf)

Samir / team — quick pricing note from my side after reviewing Rachel's MAP draft:
- We can support the $600k first-year commit if NovaProd agrees to the staged discount matrix in the spreadsheet (5% at 50% ramp, +7% at 80% ramp).
- Proposal to add an "acceleration credit" clause: if NovaProd exceeds target usage by 20% within 30 days of a sweep, Redwood applies a one-time $20k acceleration credit that counts toward the first-year commit. This gives a small incentive to push load tests earlier.
- For AWS Private Offer lines: split into three SKUs — Eval Credits (non-billable until converted), Pilot Consumption, and Annual Commitment (pre-paid or invoiced monthly).

Operational ask: Marcus, can the billing ops team show how the eval-credit conversion will appear on an AWS invoice and whether it requires an upfront Vendor Settlement mapping?

Ben Carter
Head, Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference

Team / Samir — from a billing and procurement standpoint a couple clarifications needed before we spin up a Private Offer: 
- Doc/PO items needed: a) Statement of Work (short) referencing MAP milestones, b) PO template with billing contact, c) payment terms (Net 30 default; willing to consider Net 45 for initial pilot).
- DocuSign flow: we prefer to attach the MAP as an exhibit to the Private Offer contract and route the PO through DocuSign. Samir, is procurement comfortable with DocuSign? If not, we can route via email and a vendor form.
- Legal ask: include SOC2 summary and data processing addendum in the package. Rachel, I'll add the standard DPA language to the PO draft and drop a DocuSign link once we have final amounts.

Lauren Bishop

Thanks everyone — this is a helpful framework. Procurement is okay with DocuSign and wants the MAP included as an exhibit. A few practical items from our side before we sign: 
- Procurement window: we can commit to a first-year $600k TCV if the Day 60 sweep shows >=80% of target RPS. If Day 60 is at 60–79% we move to a $350k pro-rated commit with a 3% discount (instead of higher tiers).
- Approvals: internal finance needs a sample invoice showing eval-credit conversions and the AWS PO line items. Marcus, can you share a sample? (procurement@novaprod.com)
- Timeline: we want the DocuSign packet by Mon Aug 23 to close legal/finance reviews by Aug 31. Can Redwood deliver?

If you can get the Private Offer draft + DocuSign bundle by EOD Mon, we’ll start internal approval concurrently.
